title: A new arrival
hook: A label about origin answers one question, not every question.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: A species is living outside its native range. Does that fact alone establish that it is invasive and harmful?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: A species is living outside its native range. Does that fact alone establish that it is invasive and harmful?

claims.text: A species is living outside its native range. Does that fact alone establish that it is invasive and harmful? The first panel records location outside a native range; the second highlights the separate question of impact. A non-native species is not automatically shown to be invasive merely by its origin. Definitions and impacts need context and evidence.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: US Fish and Wildlife Service, invasive species, https://www.fws.gov/

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
An introduced plant has not yet been studied for its impact. Can its harmfulness be concluded from introduction alone? Being introduced does not by itself establish an impact.
